open_points.subject: State 0 acceptance
open_points.text: “Reopened by the owner on 2026-10-27” and “State 0 closes again when its question rounds are clear; the owner then accepts it as a whole,” while “None open” says all question rounds are answered
open_points.question: Is the reopened State 0 accepted as a whole, or is owner acceptance still pending?
options: Accepted as a whole after R0-67
Still reopened and awaiting explicit acceptance
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as still reopened until an explicit acceptance decision is recorded.

open_points.subject: Pre-R0-24 frontend references
open_points.text: “In decisions before R0-24, ‘the Registry frontend’ reads ‘the owner interface’” conflicts with R0-13’s later note that “both are retired,” while R0-29 creates and retains the owner interface
open_points.question: Does the blanket substitution apply to R0-13, or does “both are retired” mean only the old frontend and `onboard_object`?
options: Exclude R0-13’s retirement note from the substitution
Apply the substitution literally, retiring the owner interface too
open_points.default_guess: Treat the retirement as applying to the old frontend and `onboard_object`, not the owner interface.

open_points.subject: Production host trust boundary
open_points.text: R0-28 calls the home server “a machine on which no agent runs,” while R0-48 says “The agent runs in a separate VM Agent on the same server”
open_points.question: Is the no-agent boundary the physical home server or only VM Platform?
options: No agent runs in VM Platform, but it may run in VM Agent on the same physical server
No agent may run anywhere on the physical home server
open_points.default_guess: Apply the boundary to VM Platform and allow the agent in the isolated VM Agent.

open_points.subject: Non-production instance classification
open_points.text: “Test instances — any other instance … Each holds its own identity space and no production personal data,” but the VPS is an explicit migration source and may be the running instance holding the production data being migrated
open_points.question: What actor and trust boundary covers the legacy VPS source during migration, and may it contain production personal data?
options: Treat the legacy VPS as a separate migration-source actor allowed to contain production data
Treat it as a test instance and require its export to contain no production personal data
open_points.default_guess: Treat the legacy VPS as a temporary trusted migration source distinct from test instances.

open_points.subject: Permitted import sources
open_points.text: “nothing moves between an instance and production except by an explicit import” applies to any test instance, while the import action permits only “the VPS or the test rig”
open_points.question: Can developer-laptop and agent-machine instances ever be imported, or are VPS and test rig the exhaustive sources?
options: Only VPS and test rig may be imported
Any test instance may be imported explicitly
open_points.default_guess: Limit production imports to the two named sources.

open_points.subject: Agent projection confidentiality
open_points.text: The agent “never receives a `personal_data` value,” but its projection contains “display name, status, rooms and artifact pointers,” whose names, `uri`, `payload_ref` and digest values have no stated rule preventing personal data
open_points.question: What guarantees that project and room names or artifact-pointer values exposed to an agent contain no personal data?
options: Prohibit and validate personal data in all agent-visible fields
Omit or redact unsafe values from the agent projection
Classify these values as safe by governance without runtime validation
open_points.default_guess: Define agent-visible fields as non-personal inputs and reject values that violate that constraint.

open_points.subject: Company customer name
open_points.text: Recording a company customer requires “name,” while “Fiscal customer data (NIF, legal name): PresuPro owns it”
open_points.question: For a Customer whose kind is `company`, what Registry name is required if the company’s legal name belongs exclusively to PresuPro?
options: A non-legal display or contact name
The legal name despite the exclusion
No name for company customers
open_points.default_guess: Use a distinct non-fiscal display name and keep the legal name in PresuPro.

open_points.subject: Session access concurrency
open_points.text: The session access output includes “the access version,” and R0-29 says “a change made against an older revision is refused,” but grant, revoke, active-project change and request-answer actions do not say whether they take the access version or what stale input does
open_points.question: Which session-access mutations require an expected access version, and what happens on a stale version?
options: Every owner mutation of session access requires the current access version
Only selected mutations use the version
The version is informational and mutations do not perform stale checks
open_points.default_guess: Require the current access version for every owner mutation of session access and refuse stale changes atomically.

open_points.subject: Answering an access request
open_points.text: Granting “adds the project the owner picks from the catalogue,” but the only stated failure is “a request no longer pending refused”
open_points.question: What happens if the selected project is unknown, archived, anonymised, deleted, or already granted when the owner answers the request?
options: Apply the same eligibility rules as the separate grant action
Allow any catalogue selection, including archived projects
Clear the request but decline the invalid grant
open_points.default_guess: Apply the grant action’s eligibility rules and leave the request pending if the answer is refused.

open_points.subject: Customer restriction transitions
open_points.text: The action marks a Customer “restricted, or no longer restricted,” but gives only “unknown or erased customer refused”
open_points.question: What is the observable result of restricting an already restricted customer or lifting a restriction that is not present, and do these no-op requests move the customer revision?
options: Return unchanged and do not move the revision
Return unchanged and move the revision
Refuse the invalid transition
open_points.default_guess: Return the unchanged Customer and do not move its revision.

open_points.subject: Customer relationship date and transitions
open_points.text: The Customer is “marked as ended on that date, or the mark cleared,” but the text does not identify who supplies the date or what repeated end/resume requests do
open_points.question: Is the end date owner-supplied or Registry-generated, and what happens when ending an already ended relationship or resuming one that is not ended?
options: Owner supplies the effective date; repeated transitions are unchanged
Registry records the action time; repeated transitions are unchanged
Repeated or state-inapplicable transitions are refused
open_points.default_guess: Let the owner supply the effective end date and make repeated transitions unchanged without moving the revision.

open_points.subject: Anonymised project re-erasure
open_points.text: An anonymised project keeps “its id, status and artifact pointers,” remains `archived`, and is never listed, while “erase an archived project” also permits deletion whole
open_points.question: May an anonymised project later be erased again and deleted whole, and if so how can the owner select it through the owner interface when project reads only answer that it was erased and lists omit it?
options: Allow later whole deletion by retained project id
Make anonymisation final and refuse further erasure
Expose anonymised records in a dedicated owner retention view
open_points.default_guess: Allow later whole deletion by retained project id through the retention/audit view.

open_points.subject: Audit coverage
open_points.text: R0-37 promises a log of “significant changes of state” with an acting principal including “agent through Kernel,” while R0-58 says “Ordinary reads, agent calls and the inner steps of flows are not recorded” and lists only some state changes
open_points.question: Exactly which state-changing actions are audited: room additions, artifact publication and withdrawal, session registration, active-project changes, access requests and answers, imports, archives, and refused attempts?
options: Audit every accepted state change but no reads or refused attempts
Audit only the categories explicitly enumerated in R0-58
Audit accepted and refused significant mutation attempts
open_points.default_guess: Audit every accepted state change, including agent-initiated changes, but not reads or refused attempts.

open_points.subject: Audit outcome field
open_points.text: Audit entries include “the outcome,” but Registry “records only significant changes of state,” which excludes a refused operation that changes no state
open_points.question: Does `outcome` describe only the result of an accepted change, or are refused mutation attempts also audit entries?
options: Only accepted changes are logged, with their accepted outcome
Refused significant mutations are logged too
Only selected security-relevant refusals are logged
open_points.default_guess: Log only accepted state changes and use `outcome` to describe the accepted result.
